SmartCity summary
As a city manager in the SmartCity simulation, your goal is to turn a traditional town into a modern SmartCity that is attractive for both residents and businesses. So your goal is to reach the highest SmartCity index that is possible! Competing cities in the region are also working towards this goal. Beyond the SmartCity Index, factors such as the mobility of residents and businesses play a crucial role in the success of your town. The SmartCity index, the main performance indicator of the simulation, is composed of several sub-indices and factors, which are listed below. Open the manual for more details.
SmartCity index =Economy * 0.25 +Environment * 0.2 +Governance * 0.15 +Living conditions * 0.15 +Mobility * 0.1 +People * 0.15

City overview
Economic Development

This category covers projects aimed at developing the city's economy. Their goal is to improve the quality of urban infrastructure and services and to raise residents' quality of life.

1 - Neighbourhood Economy Model
Why should you cross the whole city for everything when it can be done locally? The project supports the creation of local small markets, community gardens, repair workshops, family services and community enterprises. Residential communities can shape their surroundings based on their own ideas and needs, while new jobs and more accessible services are created. The development strengthens neighbourhood ties and can save residents time and money.

2 - Commercial and Cultural Centre
A vibrant city centre with an international atmosphere is created, where commerce, culture and community life meet. The development expands the existing commercial district with modern shops, restaurants, services, residential buildings and community spaces. Public spaces are renewed, pedestrian and transport connections improve, and the area becomes tidier and more liveable. The investment creates new jobs, supports local businesses and makes the area more liveable and attractive.

3 - Local Food Supply
By modernising the four existing farmers' markets and expanding their range, fresh local food becomes available in more places. New sales points, refrigeration and storage facilities are built, and an online marketplace enables pre-ordering and local pick-up. Regular gastronomic and family programmes make the markets more attractive. The development increases local producers' revenues, creates new sales opportunities and jobs, reduces food transport needs and makes shopping more convenient for residents.

What is waste for one company can be a valuable raw material for another! Within the project, the municipality and local companies set up a joint system for recycling industrial by-products, waste and surplus energy. New collection, processing and material-exchange solutions are launched, reducing landfilling, energy consumption and pollution. The development lowers businesses' operating costs and creates new business opportunities and green jobs.
